content: Internal Revenue Service, Compliance Division. This call is being recorded for legal purposes. Is this Taylor Morgan?
Uh, yes, this is Taylor. Why are you calling me?

Taylor, you were selected for review due to discrepancies in your recent tax filings, specifically relating to cryptocurrency activity. Are you aware of the reporting requirements for digital assets on your federal returns?
No, I... I just graduated last year. I don't really know much about crypto taxes, I thought I only had my W-2.

Our records indicate multiple unreported transactions involving Bitcoin and Ethereum over the past two years. The IRS takes crypto asset concealment very seriously, this is classified as felony tax evasion.
Wait, felony? I, I didn't know I had to do anything special. Is this like, going to ruin my credit?

Taylor, failure to comply can trigger criminal charges, asset seizure, and immediate wage garnishment. If you want to avoid further escalation, I need to verify your identity so we can discuss resolution options. Can you confirm your date of birth and last four digits of your Social Security Number?
Um, it's 08/15/2000, and the last four are 2147. Please don't freeze my bank account, I have student loans,

As long as you cooperate fully, we can try to resolve this outside of court. However, you should know that an indictment notice has already been drafted, and your file is being reviewed for potential asset forfeiture as of this morning.
No, please, I can't go to court. What do I have to do to fix this? I can't pay a lawyer or anything.

There is a settlement opportunity available right now, but only if you act immediately. If you delay or discuss this with anyone, your case will be flagged for prosecution and your accounts will be frozen by the Treasury Department.
Okay, okay, I won't tell anyone. What do I have to do? How much is this about?

Your total compliance fine for unreported crypto is $3,700. This must be paid today to prevent arrest and further penalties. Because of the nature of the violation, the IRS is only accepting settlement via wire transfer, Bitcoin wallet, or prepaid gift cards at this time.
I really don't have that much money! I only have a little in my checking account and maybe $500 on my credit card.

Taylor, I want to help you, but if you cannot pay in full, the minimum I can accept to pause legal action is $1,200 as an initial installment. Do you have access to that amount between your cards and bank account?
Maybe if I move things around, but I'd need to transfer some from my savings.

Good. Here's what you need to do: Go to the nearest pharmacy or supermarket and purchase $1,200 worth of Apple or Google Play gift cards. Once you have them, remain on this line and read me each code on the back. Do not hang up or talk to anyone at the store about this IRS settlement, or your case will automatically escalate.
Wait, is this really normal? Gift cards for the IRS?

This is a special compliance process for digital asset violations. The cards serve as secured payment tokens, and you will receive a confirmation email for your records. If you fail to comply within the next 45 minutes, the federal warrant for your arrest will be activated.
Oh my God, okay. I guess I'll go to CVS right now. Can I use my credit card for this?
Yes. Buy as many $100 cards as you can up to $1,200. Stay on the line with me while you make the purchase. When you return to your car, I'll give you further instructions.
Okay, I'm heading there now. Please don't arrest me. I really can't have anything happen to my credit.
Follow my instructions and everything will be fine. Remember, do NOT speak to anyone about the situation or the IRS will be forced to proceed with asset seizure.
I understand. I'm going now. Please just wait for me to get the cards.
